children: The benchmark KOSPI fell more than 2% to around 5,880 on Thursday, reversing the previous session’s sharp rally as investors took profits and losses in heavyweight stocks weighed on the index.
LG Energy Solution (-8.34%), Hanwha Aerospace (-6.48%), and Samsung Electronics (-0.62%) led the declines, offsetting gains in SK Hynix (+3.83%) and SK Square (+3.26%).

Sentiment was also dampened by Samsung Electronics’ latest earnings, as its semiconductor division reported operating profit of 106.5 trillion won in the third quarter, below analysts’ expectations of 108.5 trillion won, tempering optimism over sustained AI-driven demand.
Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rate at 3.75–4.00% in a 10–2 vote, leaving the interest rate differential with South Korea at up to 1 percentage point.
Domestic sentiment offered some positive signals, with the Bank of Korea’s Composite Business Sentiment Index rising 5.1 points to 104.2 in October, its highest level since August 2022.

title: South Korean Shares Drop on Profit-Taking
